question: Compare ROA, efficiency ratio and noncurrent loan rate for M&T, Citizens Financial Group, KeyCorp and Huntington in 2026Q2. Who leads on profitability?
headline: M&T leads on profitability in 2026Q2 with a 1.53% quarterly ROA, while KeyCorp posts the lowest efficiency ratio (54.90%) and noncurrent loan rate (0.86%) of the four.
insights: ROA (quarterly, annualized): M&T 1.53%, KeyCorp 1.28%, Huntington 1.13%, Citizens Financial Group 1.03%; the four-company aggregate is 1.23%.

Efficiency ratio (lower is better): KeyCorp 54.90%, M&T 55.69%, Citizens 60.61%, Huntington 61.70%; the group aggregate is 58.42%. Huntington is flagged as a merger quarter, so its income ratios may be distorted.

Noncurrent loan rate (lower is better): KeyCorp 0.86%, Huntington 1.06%, M&T 1.35%, Citizens 1.36%; the group aggregate is 1.17%. M&T, which leads on ROA, has the second-highest noncurrent rate, just below Citizens.

question: Which FDIC regions improved ROA the most from 2025Q2 to 2026Q2, and did their efficiency ratios improve too?
headline: Atlanta improved ROA the most, rising 0.63 percentage points from 0.65% in 2025Q2 to 1.29% in 2026Q2 (quarterly, annualized). Every region with a known ROA gained, but efficiency ratios moved in different directions.
insights: Ranked by ROA gain: Atlanta +0.63 pp, Chicago +0.17 pp, New York +0.16 pp, San Francisco +0.13 pp, Dallas +0.12 pp, Kansas City +0.08 pp. San Francisco still has the highest 2026Q2 ROA at 1.73%.
Efficiency ratio (lower is better) improved in Atlanta (-1.74 pp to 54.71%), Kansas City (-2.12 pp to 53.80%), Dallas (-1.25 pp to 56.60%) and New York (-0.88 pp to 57.84%).
Chicago's ROA gain came with a worse efficiency ratio, up 2.05 pp to 57.55%. San Francisco's efficiency ratio edged up 0.23 pp to 56.82%.
The Unknown group (banks with no institution record) is excluded from rankings. Its efficiency ratio improved 5.79 pp, and its ROA rose 0.55 pp.

question: How has industry ROA trended since 2024?
headline: Industry quarterly ROA rose from 1.12% in 2024Q4 to 1.37% in 2026Q2, a gain of 0.26 percentage points.
insights: The series rose in most quarters: 1.12% (2024Q4), 1.15% (2025Q1), 1.13% (2025Q2), 1.27% (2025Q3), 1.24% (2025Q4), 1.24% (2026Q1), then 1.37% (2026Q2), the highest in the period shown.
The biggest single step-up came in 2025Q3 (up 0.14 points from 2025Q2), and the 2026Q2 reading is 0.13 points above 2026Q1.

These are annualized quarterly ROA figures for all FDIC filers (aggregate, sum of net income over sum of quarter-end assets). 2024Q3 is not shown because quarterly income needs prior-year-to-date data.

question: Loan-to-deposit ratio trend by banking organization for New England organizations with $10B-$50B in assets since 2024
headline: Three New England banking organizations with $10B-$50B in assets had loan-to-deposit ratios between about 89% and 96% in 2026Q2, after Beacon Financial's ratio fell from 103.17% in 2024Q3.
insights: Beacon Financial Corp fell from 103.17% (2024Q3) to 95.57% (2026Q2), a change of -7.60 percentage points, the largest decline of the three.
Eastern Bankshares rose from 87.43% to 89.21% over the same period (+1.78 points), and Independent Bank Corp (MA) eased from 92.47% to 89.72% (-2.74 points).

All three ratios stayed in a narrow band through 2025 and 2026, with Eastern and Independent moving within about 3 points of each other since 2025Q1. Independent Bank Corp (MA) was marginally above Beacon in 2025Q4 (91.52% vs 91.47%).
